venue: Truist Park (Smyrna / Cumberland, Cobb County, GA). CONFIRMED current as of August 2026: RateYourSeats event listings for August 2026 show Braves home games at 'Truist Park - Atlanta, GA'; MLB.com and Ballparks of Baseball both list Truist Park as the Atlanta Braves home ballpark. Opened 2017 as SunTrust Park; renamed Truist Park in January 2020 after the SunTrust/BB&T merger. No further rename or relocation found for 2026. NOTE: many RateYourSeats photo filenames and the RYS internal master_id still say 'suntrust-park-smyrna-ga' — that is legacy naming, not a current venue name.
concert_only_sections: Field Sections (concert floor) — https://www.rateyourseats.com/truist-park/seating/field-seatss states verbatim: 'Field seats for a concert at Truist Park...' and 'Floor sections are typically labeled alphabetically, with sections beginning with A located closest to the stage and sections beginning with B behind them. For certain events, there may be a General Admission (GA) Pit directly in front of the stage.' The specific floor section labels (e.g. A1, B2) are NOT enumerated by the source — UNKNOWN. This entry is a concert-only floor and is deliberately excluded from 'sections'.

NOTE: 'General Admission' and 'Standing Room Only' also appear in the RYS section index but are zone links, not numbered ticketed baseball sections; they are excluded from 'sections'. Whether SRO is baseball-only, concert-only or both was not established — UNKNOWN.
capacity: CONFLICTING FIGURES. (a) 41,084 — stated by theshadium.com/blog/shaded-seats-truist-park ('The stadium's capacity is 41,084') and reported as the current Wikipedia figure in web search. (b) 41,500 — stated by ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/truist-park ('The ballpark has a seating capacity of 41,500'). (c) 41,147 — reported by web search as an alternate figure from some sources; no primary URL captured. RECOMMENDED: 41,084 (most commonly cited current figure and matches Wikipedia). Ballparks of Baseball's 41,500 appears to be the original 2017 announced capacity.

orientation.batter_faces: Southeast. Center field points toward the southeast; the batter at home plate faces southeast. Consequently the first-base-side stands face roughly northeast (and get afternoon shade first), while the third-base-side stands face roughly southwest into the afternoon sun.
orientation.confidence: medium — two independent sources agree on southeast, and the shade behaviour cross-checks against RateYourSeats, but one earlier web-search summary asserted the opposite (northeast). See 'uncertain'.
orientation.source: https://theshadium.com/blog/shaded-seats-truist-park — verbatim: 'Truist Park's orientation is approximately 135° (SE), positioning center field toward the southeast with home plate facing northwest. This orientation places the first base side roughly northeast-facing, away from the afternoon sun that dominates from the south and southwest.' CROSS-CHECK (independent, agrees): web search of intheballparks.com / shadedseats.com states Truist Park 'is oriented to the southeast' and that it was built off the MLB-ideal east-northeast alignment because of terrain and pre-existing gas lines. CROSS-CHECK (geometry, agrees): https://www.rateyourseats.com/truist-park/seating/terrace-infield — 'For afternoon games, the first base side (Sections 216–218) typically receives shade earlier than the sections along the third base side.'

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE FROM THE FIRST-BASE SIDE TOWARD THE THIRD-BASE SIDE, then continue around the outfield from left field through center field to right field. On a standard seating chart drawn with home plate at the bottom and the outfield at the top, the numbers run CLOCKWISE. Within every infield tier: LOW numbers = first base / right field side; HIGH numbers = third base / left field side; the middle of each hundred-series sits behind home plate. Concretely: field level 10-21 = first base line, 22-30 = behind home plate, 31-42 = third base line; lower level 110-121 = first base line, 122-130 = behind home plate, 131-142 = third base line (an exact +100 mirror of the field level, which is a strong internal consistency check); 200 level 216-218 = first base line, 220-231 = behind home plate, 233-238 = third base line; 300 level home plate at 325-327; 400 level home plate at 425-427. Past the third-base end the lower level keeps climbing around the outfield: 144 sits at the LEFT field foul pole, 144-155 sweep left field -> center -> right-center, and 156-160 (Chop House) finish in RIGHT field, closing the ring next to 107-109 which sit at the right field foul pole. Truist Club sections 1-9 are a separate innermost field-level arc directly behind home plate with section 5 dead centre.

numbering_direction.confidence: high — five independent RateYourSeats zone pages plus two section-page anchors all agree, the field level and 100 level are an exact +100 mirror of each other, the outfield wrap (144 at LF pole -> 155 at RCF -> 156-160 in RF) closes the ring cleanly against 107-109 at the RF pole, and the dugout sides and afternoon-shade behaviour independently corroborate that low numbers are the first base side.

home_plate_sections._notes: Every tier at Truist Park DOES wrap behind home plate — no tier needs its anchor omitted. accessibility.summary: Truist Park was designed to be universally accessible. Accessible seating with wheelchair spaces and companion seats is available on multiple levels, located near elevators or ramps and close to accessible restrooms and concessions. The ballpark provides accessible parking, elevators and escalators, courtesy rides, accessible restrooms and lowered concession counters. Complimentary wheelchair escort service is offered from the gates to seats and back. Priority for elevator use is given to guests with disabilities and elderly guests. Accessible parking in Lot N29 is served by a shuttle that picks up and drops off on Battery Avenue just outside the Third Base Gate. The Accessible Seating Department can be reached at (404) 577-9100 (Option 5) or accessibleservices@braves.com. RateYourSeats records wheelchair positions behind the last numbered row in at least some lower-level sections, e.g. Section 133: 'Wheelchair seating is available behind Row 18.' CAVEAT: the Braves' own accessibility pages (mlb.com/braves/ballpark/information/accessibility and mlb.com/braves/ballpark/disability-access-guide) could not be read directly in this session — the first returned an empty body and the second exceeded the fetch size limit — so the above is assembled from web-search extracts of those Braves pages plus MobiliQuest. Verify against the Braves pages before publishing.

row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE NUMBERED, not lettered, in every section inspected — no lettered rows were observed anywhere at Truist Park. Confirmed row ranges from RateYourSeats section pages: Section 107 'Rows in Section 107 are labeled 1-8'; Section 114 'labeled 1-20'; Section 133 'labeled 1-18, 19-20' (a split range); Section 142 'labeled 1-20'; Section 160 (Chop House Terrace) 'labeled 1-5'. Per-level row counts from zone pages: Truist Club (1-9) has four rows per section, except Section 9 which has five; Dugout Club seats are all 'within roughly the first 15 rows from the field'; Terrace Infield sections 'contain about 19 numbered rows, with entry tunnels located at the very top of the section'; Vista Infield sections have 'at least 7 rows and no more than 13 rows'; Chop House Terrace sections have five rows. 400-level Grandstand row ranges — UNKNOWN. Section entrances are commonly at the TOP of the section: 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 20' (Sections 114, 142) and 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 20' with wheelchair seating behind Row 18 (Section 133). ACCESSIBLE-ROW LABEL CONVENTION (WC / WCH / VWC / AC suffix etc.) — UNKNOWN. No source consulted used any such label; RateYourSeats describes accessible positions positionally instead ('Wheelchair seating is available behind Row 18'). SEAT NUMBERING: see seat1_side_verbatim — seat 1 is on the right when facing the field, i.e. seat numbers increase in the same rotational direction as section numbers (from the first base side toward the third base side).
seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the stage/field, lower number seats are on the right" — quoted verbatim from the 'Row Numbers' block of RateYourSeats section pages. Observed identically, with no variation, on all five section pages fetched: https://www.rateyourseats.com/truist-park/seating/sections/107 , /sections/114 , /sections/133 , /sections/142 and /sections/160. These span the lower level down the first base line (107, 114), the lower level infield on the third base side (133), the lower level down the third base line (142) and the Chop House in right field (160), so the rule appears to be park-wide. No contradicting statement was found in any source. NOT independently verified for the field level (1-42), the 200, 300 or 400 levels — those section pages were not individually fetched.
known_obstructions: PROTECTIVE NETTING: RateYourSeats fan feedback on Section 133 states verbatim: 'Front of sections 118-133 are behind the netting — There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 118-133. The height and coverage of netting or screening will vary by section.' Separately, the Dugout Club page states: 'Protective netting is installed in front of these sections, which helps protect fans but can reduce the chances of catching a foul ball' — referring to field-level Sections 10-21 and 31-42. Taken together the netting covers at least field-level 10-42 and lower-level 118-133. Whether the net now extends all the way to the foul poles (as at many parks) is NOT stated by any source consulted — UNKNOWN; no official Braves netting statement was successfully fetched. OTHER OBSTRUCTED/PARTIAL VIEWS: 'Below the Chop' group area in right field — 'Fans in this section watch the game through openings in the outfield fence, creating a very unique field-level viewing perspective.' Chop House views 'focus primarily on the right field and outfield portions of the game' and are 'not as direct as seats near the dugouts.' Lower-level sections nearer the corner bases 'will have you facing more towards center field and leave you with a fairly significant head turn to see the pitchers mound and home plate.' No pole/railing obstruction reports were found. SUN/COVER (not an obstruction but relevant): rows 8 and above are under cover in lower-level down-the-line sections (114, 133, 142); the Home Run Porch is mostly full sun except around Row 12 of Sections 144-145; the 400 level has a 90-foot-wide canopy over the upper deck.
uncertain: VENUE NAME: no rename found — Truist Park is current for 2026. However RateYourSeats' internal master_id is still 'suntrust-park-smyrna-ga' and most of its photo filenames say 'SunTrust-Park-...'. Do not let that legacy string leak into generated copy.

CITY: sources disagree on the city. RateYourSeats meta-description says 'Truist Park in Smyrna, GA' and Ballparks of Baseball lists '-Location: Smyrna, GA', but RateYourSeats' own event listings say 'Truist Park - Atlanta, GA'. The ballpark is physically in unincorporated Cobb County near Smyrna, marketed as Atlanta. Pick one deliberately.

CAPACITY: three figures in circulation — 41,084 (Wikipedia / theshadium), 41,500 (Ballparks of Baseball, likely the 2017 announced figure) and 41,147 (reported by search, no primary URL captured). Recommended 41,084.

ORIENTATION: theshadium.com states 135 degrees / centre field to the SOUTHEAST, and intheballparks/shadedseats independently say Truist Park 'is oriented to the southeast'. But an earlier web-search summary asserted 'approximately 45 degrees (NE) ... third base side roughly northwest-facing', which is the exact opposite. Southeast is preferred because it is the one that cross-checks against the observed shade behaviour (RateYourSeats: first base side 216-218 gets shade earlier than the third base side). Also note RateYourSeats' Lower Level Down the Line review says 'opt for seats towards the right field corner which will leaving you facing the east' — under a southeast orientation right-field-corner seats would face roughly north-northwest, not east, so that RYS sentence does not reconcile with either compass claim. Treat compass detail as low confidence.

SECTION INDEX GAPS: the RateYourSeats section index omits numbers that its own zone pages imply exist — 129 (Delta Sky360 Executive is described as 'Sections 122–130'), 221 (Xfinity Club is 'Sections 220–231'), 319/321/332 (Vista Infield is 'Sections 318–333') and 419/421/432 (Grandstand Infield is 'Sections 418–433'). Also missing from the index: 115, 117, 119, 121, 132, 134, 136, 139, 219, 232, 234, 236, 334, 336, 338, 434, 436, 441. Some of these are probably real sections RateYourSeats simply has no page for; others may genuinely not exist. The 'sections' array above lists ONLY what the index actually contains. Reconcile against the official Braves seating chart before publishing.

TRUIST CLUB 1-9 DIRECTION: no source states which end of the 1-9 arc is the first base side. Section 5 is confirmed dead centre behind the plate and 4 and 6 are 'just to either side'. By consistency with the rest of the park section 1 would be the first base end and 9 the third base end, but that is an INFERENCE — do not publish it as fact without a source.

LOWER-LEVEL HOME-PLATE CENTRE: no source names a single 100-level section as 'directly behind home plate'. 122-130 is quoted as the behind-the-plate block and 118-133 is the quoted netting range; 125/126 is the arithmetic centre and the +100 mirror of the confirmed field-level 25/26, but is an inference.
BULLPENS: RateYourSeats says the Braves bullpen is beneath Sections 153-154; a secondary source says 152-153. Both agree the visiting bullpen is at 144-145.
VISITING DUGOUT EXTENT: RateYourSeats says Sections 31-35 are behind the visitor dugout; a secondary source says 31-34.
NETTING EXTENT: only 118-133 (lower level) and 10-42 (field level) are sourced. Whether netting now runs to the foul poles is UNKNOWN — no official Braves statement was retrievable.

ACCESSIBLE ROW LABELS: no source uses WC / WCH / VWC or an AC suffix at Truist Park. Accessible positions are described positionally ('Wheelchair seating is available behind Row 18'). The actual ticketed row label for accessible seats is UNKNOWN.

OFFICIAL BRAVES PAGES NOT DIRECTLY READ: https://www.mlb.com/braves/ballpark/information/accessibility returned an empty body and https://www.mlb.com/braves/ballpark/disability-access-guide and https://www.mlb.com/braves/ballpark/information/guide both exceeded the fetch size limit. Accessibility and policy content above is therefore second-hand via web-search extracts. The Wikipedia article on Truist Park also exceeded the fetch limit and was not read directly.

CONCERT FLOOR LABELS: RateYourSeats describes the concert floor as alphabetically labelled (A-sections nearest the stage, B-sections behind, possible GA Pit) but does not enumerate the labels, so concert_only_sections could not be listed as discrete section IDs.

GENERAL ADMISSION / STANDING ROOM ONLY: these appear as zones in the RYS section index with no numbered sections attached. Whether either applies to Braves baseball games and which physical areas they map to was not established.
